stem:
Myra watches a breathing model: balloons for the lungs and a rubber sheet for the diaphragm. When the rubber sheet moves down and the rib space widens, the balloons inflate.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: This model step matches inhalation: ribs move up and out, the diaphragm moves down, and air is drawn in.
The rubber sheet represents the diaphragm, not the lungs.
The rubber sheet represents the lungs.
Every breathing animal inhales only by moving ribs up and out and the diaphragm down in this same way.

teacher.key_rationale: Inhalation widens the chest as ribs rise and the diaphragm descends; in the model the rubber sheet is the diaphragm. Calling the sheet the lungs, or forcing every animal into this exact pattern, miss that hinge.
